objective: By the end of this lesson you can write, from memory and from AC 61-65K, the logbook entries and endorsements a CFI gives (training given, pre-solo, solo, solo cross-country, Class B, complex, high-performance, tailwheel, practical test recommendations and flight reviews), keep the records 14 CFR 61.189 requires, keep your own instructor privileges current, and teach all of it to a new instructor.
why: Your signature is what lets a student fly alone, lets an applicant sit for a checkride and lets a pilot keep acting as pilot in command. Endorsements mark privileges granted and limitations incurred, and using the recommended wording lowers the chance that someone flies without a prerequisite or misreads a limit [[12:4|AC 61-65K 3]]. The FAA may hold an instructor accountable for an endorsement given to a pilot who does not meet the rules [[25:184|AIH 9-14]].

prereading.what: Practical test prerequisites, retests, and the student pilot pre-solo, solo, cross-country and Class B rules.
prereading.label: AC 61-65K 7 to 14

prereading.what: The sample endorsements themselves, plus the required signature block (RE end date).
prereading.label: AC 61-65K A-7 to A-21

prereading.what: Flight instructor recent experience, the 24-calendar-month period, and reinstatement of privileges.
prereading.label: AC 61-65K 22 to 26

prereading.what: Logging training time, instructor records, and the limits on what you may endorse.
prereading.label: 14 CFR 61.51, 61.189, 61.195

prereading.what: The regulations behind every student pilot endorsement.
prereading.label: 14 CFR 61.87 to 61.95

prereading.what: The instructor's responsibility for recommendations, records, flight reviews and checkouts.
prereading.label: AIH 9-13 to 9-14, C-1 to C-4

prereading.what: How a flight review is run and what to log when it is, or is not, satisfactory.
prereading.label: AC 61-98E 4-1 to 4-8

warmup: Think first: a student shows up with a logbook full of your colleague's signatures. Every endorsement is there, but one says nothing about make and model, one was signed 95 days ago, and none lists any limits. Which of these would stop the student from flying solo today, and which only feel wrong?

key_terms.def: A written, signed entry showing that a pilot received training or was granted a privilege or limitation, usually made by a CFI [[1:31|PHAK 1-16]] [[12:4|AC 61-65K 3]].
A ground or flight instructor acting within the privileges of their certificate and current under 61.217 or 61.197, or a person the Administrator authorizes [[12:30|AC 61-65K 37]].
The last day of a flight instructor's 24-calendar-month recent experience period. It goes in every signature block on a certificate without an expiration date [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].
Flight time in which the student is the sole occupant of the aircraft [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(a)]].
The specific aircraft named in solo endorsements; the 90-day solo endorsement is for the specific make and model to be flown [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]].
A whole month counted to its last day. Practical test training must fall within 2 calendar months before the month of application [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)]].
At least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training covering part 91 and the maneuvers the instructor judges necessary [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]].
The Airman Certificate and/or Rating Application. It carries the instructor's written recommendation for a practical test [[25:183|AIH 9-13]].
The FAA's online certification and rating application system. It checks entries and reduces errors compared with paper forms [[25:203|AIH C-2]].
Flight instructor refresher course. Completing one within the preceding 3 calendar months is one way to establish recent experience [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(b)(2)(iii)]].
An airplane with an engine of more than 200 horsepower [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(f)]].
The FAA Aviation English Language Standard. A pilot who does not meet it on a flight review or IPC does not get a completion endorsement [[12:8|AC 61-65K 11.4.2]].

body.p: Only a flight instructor with the right rating may give the training that qualifies someone for solo and solo cross-country, endorse an applicant for a pilot certificate or rating, endorse a logbook to show training given, or endorse a logbook for solo privileges [[60:190|14 CFR 61.3(d)(2)]]. 14 CFR 61.193 lists what a CFI may endorse: student pilot, pilot, flight instructor and ground instructor certificates, aircraft and instrument ratings, flight reviews, operating privileges, recency, and knowledge and practical tests [[60:345|14 CFR 61.193(a)]].

An endorsement marks an event: a privilege granted, an authorization, or a limitation incurred. Using the recommended endorsements reduces the risk that someone acts without a prerequisite or misunderstands a limit [[12:4|AC 61-65K 3]].

bullets: Every endorsement must be legible and include your signature, the date you signed, your CFI certificate number, and your RE end date or certificate expiration date, as applicable [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].
Sample format for a certificate without an expiration date: /s/ [date] J. J. Jones 987654321CFI RE 12-31-2026. Printing your name is optional [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].
The AC 61-65K wording is not mandatory word for word, but at a minimum cite the 14 CFR part 61 section that was completed [[25:202|AIH C-1]].
No rule stops you from adding a requirement of your own to an endorsement [[25:202|AIH C-1]].
You may never endorse yourself for a certificate, rating, flight review, authorization, operating privilege, practical test or knowledge test [[60:349|14 CFR 61.195(i)]].

callout.text: Carry your flight instructor certificate, or other documentation acceptable to the Administrator, in your possession or readily accessible in the aircraft when you instruct [[60:190|14 CFR 61.3(d)(1)]].

check.q: Which four items must every endorsement signature block include?
check.a: Your signature, the date of signature, your CFI certificate number, and your RE end date (or expiration date if your certificate has one) [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].

chunks.title: K1: Logging the instruction you give

body.p: You must sign the logbook of every person to whom you give flight training or ground training [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189(a)]]. The student logs the time; your entry makes it count. Training time must be logged in a logbook, endorsed legibly by the authorized instructor, and include [[60:231|14 CFR 61.51(h)(2)]]:

bullets: A description of the training given.
The length of the training lesson.
Your signature, certificate number, and certificate expiration date or recent experience end date.

body.p: Each logged flight or lesson also carries the general items: date, total flight or lesson time, departure and arrival points (or where a simulator lesson happened), aircraft or device type and identification, and the type of experience, such as flight and ground training received from an authorized instructor [[60:227|14 CFR 61.51(b)]]. Conditions of flight, such as night, actual instrument and simulated instrument, are logged too [[60:228|14 CFR 61.51(b)(3)]].

head: Situation
What your entry adds
rows: Instrument time in a simulator, FTD or ATD for a certificate or rating
You were present to observe and you sign the logbook or training record to verify the time and content [[60:230|14 CFR 61.51(g)(4)]].
You teach in actual instrument conditions
You may log instrument time yourself [[60:230|14 CFR 61.51(g)(2)]].
You serve as the authorized instructor
You may log PIC time for all of that flight time if you are rated to act as PIC of that aircraft [[60:229|14 CFR 61.51(e)(3)]].
Student logs solo PIC time
Only with a current solo endorsement under 61.87 while training for a certificate or rating [[60:229|14 CFR 61.51(e)(4)]].

callout.text: Write the description as what was taught, not just the maneuver names. A syllabus with boxes next to each item turns your entries into a running record and the basis for later endorsements [[25:150|AIH 7-6]].

check.q: A new CFI signs a student's logbook with only a signature and date. What two items are missing under 61.51(h)?
check.a: The certificate number and the expiration or RE end date in the signature, plus a description of the training and the lesson length [[60:231|14 CFR 61.51(h)(2)]].

chunks.title: K2: Pre-solo knowledge test and pre-solo training

body.p: Before solo, the student must pass a knowledge test that covers applicable sections of parts 61 and 91, the airspace rules and procedures for the airport where the solo will happen, and the flight characteristics and operating limits of the make and model to be flown [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(b)]].

callout.text: You, the student's authorized instructor, must administer the pre-solo knowledge test and, at the end, review all incorrect answers with the student before authorizing solo [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(b)(2)]].

body.p: Pre-solo flight training: the student must have received and logged flight training on the maneuvers and procedures for the make and model, and demonstrated satisfactory proficiency and safety, as judged by an authorized instructor, in that or a similar make and model [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(c)]]. For a single-engine airplane the list runs from flight preparation, taxi and runups, through takeoffs and landings (normal and crosswind), stalls with recovery, emergency procedures, ground reference maneuvers, simulated engine malfunctions, slips to a landing and go-arounds [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(d)]] [[60:272|14 CFR 61.87(d)(15)]].

head: Endorsement
Rule
What it certifies
rows: Pre-solo aeronautical knowledge (A.3)
Satisfactory completion of the pre-solo knowledge test for the named make and model [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.3]].
Pre-solo flight training (A.4)
Training received and logged for that make and model, and proficiency and safety demonstrated [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.4]].
Pre-solo flight training at night (A.5)
Night takeoffs, approaches, landings and go-arounds at the solo airport, plus night navigation near it; expires 90 calendar days from the night training [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.5]].

body.p: English language: before you process a student pilot application or endorse for solo, evaluate the applicant against the AC 60-28 guidelines [[12:8|AC 61-65K 11.4.3]]. The student must meet the FAA English language standard [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.2]].

check.q: Your student scored 90 percent on the pre-solo test. What must happen before you sign A.3?
check.a: You review every incorrect answer with the student before authorizing solo [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(b)(2)]].

chunks.title: K2: The solo endorsement and its 90-day clock

body.p: A student may not fly solo without an endorsement in the logbook for the specific make and model, from an authorized instructor who gave the training within the 90 days before the flight [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]]. You may not authorize solo unless you have given the student training in that or a similar make and model, found them proficient in the 61.87 maneuvers and in the aircraft, and endorsed the logbook; it stays current only if an authorized instructor updates it every 90 days [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(p)]] [[60:278|14 CFR 61.87(p)(4)]].

head: Endorsement
Wording key
Time limit
rows: Solo, first 90-day period (A.6)
Required training received; meets 61.87(n); proficient in [M/M] [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.6]]
90 calendar days [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.3]]
Solo, each additional 90-day period (A.7)
90 calendar days
Solo at night
Night training at the solo airport and nearby navigation, by the instructor who gave it [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(o)]]
Training within the 90 days before the flight [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.4]]

bullets: The plastic student pilot certificate has no expiration date, but the endorsements that authorize solo do. They must be in the logbook whether the certificate is paper or plastic [[12:14|AC 61-65K 20.1]].
Before endorsing solo you must have given the training and decided the student can fly safely under known conditions, subject to any limits you write in the logbook [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(d)(1)]].
A student may not fly contrary to any limitation an authorized instructor placed in the logbook [[60:278|14 CFR 61.89(a)(8)]].

callout.text: Solo = Same airplane, 90-day clock, written limits. Make and model, date, and conditions in every solo endorsement.

check.q: Can the solo endorsement you gave in a C152 cover a solo in a C172?
check.a: No. The solo endorsement is for the specific make and model to be flown [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]].

chunks.title: K2: Solo cross-country, 25 NM and 50 NM

body.p: A student must meet 61.93 before a solo cross-country, any flight more than 25 nautical miles from the departure airport, or a solo landing anywhere other than the airport of origin [[60:279|14 CFR 61.93(a)(1)]]. Each cross-country needs three endorsements [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(c)]]:

bullets: Solo cross-country for the category, from the instructor who did the training (A.9) [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(c)(1)]] [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.9]].
Solo cross-country for the make and model (A.9) [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(c)(2)]].

For each flight, after reviewing the planning: names the make and model, says the planning is correct and the student is prepared under the known conditions, and that your limits are met (A.10) [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(c)(3)]] [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.10]].

body.p: Before you permit the flight you must have checked the planning, reviewed current and forecast weather and found the flight can be completed under VFR, found the student proficient, and confirmed the make and model cross-country endorsement and a current solo endorsement [[60:281|14 CFR 61.93(d)]]. The per-flight endorsement need not come from the student's usual instructor, but whoever signs must make sure the other endorsements are already there [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.6]].

head: Special case
Conditions
Endorsement
rows: Takeoffs and landings at another airport within 25 NM
You trained the student there, both directions over the route, pattern entry and exit, takeoffs and landings; purpose is takeoff and landing practice [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(b)(1)]]
A.8, listing conditions [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.8]]
Repeated solo cross-countries within 50 NM
Trained both directions over the route and at the airports; separate per-flight endorsements are not needed [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(b)(2)]]
A.11, listing conditions [[12:42|AC 61-65K A.11]]

callout.text: On every solo cross-country the student carries the logbook, the student pilot certificate and any other required record [[60:231|14 CFR 61.51(i)(2)]]. Except in an emergency, a student may land only at airports the endorsements allow [[12:17|AC 61-65K 20.12]].

check.q: Before signing the per-flight cross-country endorsement, what weather duty does 61.93(d) give you?
check.a: Review current and forecast weather and determine the flight can be completed under VFR [[60:281|14 CFR 61.93(d)(2)]].

chunks.title: K3: Other required endorsements (Class B, SFAR, aircraft)

body.p: Beyond pre-solo and solo, many privileges need a CFI's endorsement. These are the ones an ASEL instructor signs most often.

head: Endorsement
Requirement
Sample
rows: Class B airspace solo (student)
Ground and flight training on that Class B area, flight training in that specific area, endorsement dated within 90 days [[60:287|14 CFR 61.95(a)]]
Solo at an airport inside Class B (student)
Ground and flight training at that specific airport, endorsement dated within 90 days [[60:287|14 CFR 61.95(b)]]
Complex airplane
Ground and flight training, found proficient; one-time endorsement [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(e)]]
High-performance airplane (more than 200 hp)
Ground and flight training, found proficient; one-time endorsement [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(f)]] [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(f)(1)(ii)]]
Pressurized aircraft (service ceiling or max operating altitude above 25,000 ft MSL)
Ground training and endorsement [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(g)]]
Tailwheel airplane
Flight training: normal and crosswind takeoffs and landings, wheel landings unless the manufacturer recommends against them, go-arounds [[60:215|14 CFR 61.31(i)]]
Solo in an aircraft without the category/class rating
Training for that aircraft and a solo endorsement from an authorized instructor [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(d)(2)]]

body.p: SFAR endorsements: the SFAR endorsements in AC 61-65K are for SFAR 73, the Robinson R-22 and R-44 helicopter rules (ground training, solo, PIC, instructor and annual flight review endorsements) [[12:51|AC 61-65K A.60]] [[60:179|14 CFR SFAR 73]]. An ASEL instructor rarely signs them, but you should recognize that an SFAR can add its own training, endorsement and recurrent dates.

bullets: Exceptions: the complex and high-performance endorsements are not required for PIC time logged in those airplanes before August 4, 1997 [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(e)(2)]] [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(f)(2)]]. Tailwheel training is not required for PIC tailwheel time before April 15, 1991 [[60:215|14 CFR 61.31(i)(2)]].
Tailwheel training must be done with the tailwheel wheeled gear; on skis or floats the endorsement cannot be earned [[12:30|AC 61-65K 33.2]].
TSA citizenship: either keep copies of the proof of U.S. citizenship for 5 years or make the A.14 endorsement in the student's logbook and your own records [[12:42|AC 61-65K A.14]].
Students seeking sport or recreational certificates need 61.94 training and endorsement for Class B, C, D airspace and towered airports [[60:287|14 CFR 61.94(b)]].

body.p: Transition to a complex or high-performance airplane should follow a structured ground and flight syllabus run by a qualified instructor, aiming at the ACS standard for the certificate the pilot holds [[24:248|AFH 12-17]]. Treat the times in the sample syllabus as illustrations; base them on the pilot [[24:249|AFH 12-18]]. Record in the pilot's logbook the exact extent of any checkout; it protects both of you [[25:205|AIH C-4]].

check.q: A private pilot logged PIC time in a 230 hp airplane in 1995. Does she need an A.73 endorsement?
check.a: No. High-performance PIC time logged before August 4, 1997 is an exception [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(f)(2)]].

chunks.title: K4 and K4a: The practical test recommendation and initial certification

body.p: To take a practical test the applicant needs, if part 61 requires it, an endorsement from an authorized instructor certifying training received and logged within 2 calendar months before the month of application, that the applicant is prepared, and that they have shown satisfactory knowledge of the subject areas missed on the knowledge test [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)]]. The knowledge test must have been passed within the 24 calendar months before the month the practical test is completed [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(1)]].

The airman certificate application (FAA Form 8710-1) has a block for your written recommendation. Signing it is a serious responsibility: require a demonstration no less than the complete ACS procedure first [[25:183|AIH 9-13]]. Inspectors and examiners rely on your recommendation as evidence of qualification and of the knowledge-test review [[25:203|AIH C-2]]. Use IACRA when possible; it checks entries, while a mistake on paper can delay the certificate [[25:203|AIH C-2]].

head: Sub-item
Endorsements in the logbook
Application
rows: a. Initial pilot certification (e.g., private pilot ASEL)

Knowledge test: A.36 under 61.103(d) [[12:46|AC 61-65K A.36]] [[60:295|14 CFR 61.103(d)]]. Practical test: A.37 under 61.103(f) [[12:47|AC 61-65K A.37]] [[60:295|14 CFR 61.103(f)]]. Plus A.1 and A.2 under 61.39 [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.1]]. The student already has pre-solo, solo and solo cross-country endorsements the examiner will check [[1:38|PHAK 1-23]].
8710-1 (or IACRA) with your recommendation; applicant brings the knowledge test report and logbook [[1:38|PHAK 1-23]].

bullets: Initial pilot certification also needs the time limits right: all increments of a practical test must be finished within 2 calendar months after the month the test began, or the whole test is retaken [[60:221|14 CFR 61.39(g)]].

Retest after a Notice of Disapproval: a new endorsement that the applicant got the training and is prepared, and an instructor recommendation on the 8710 for each retest [[12:11|AC 61-65K 14.2]] [[60:227|14 CFR 61.49(a)]].
Letter of Discontinuance: no new endorsement; credit for passed areas lasts 60 calendar days [[12:11|AC 61-65K 14.3]].
Part 141 graduates testing with an examiner still need the 61.39(a) endorsements [[12:10|AC 61-65K 14.1]].

callout.text: Do not sign a recommendation for an applicant who has not met every regulatory requirement. Endorsing someone who does not meet the rules is a serious deficiency the FAA may hold you accountable for [[25:184|AIH 9-14]].

check.q: An applicant's last logged training was in February. What is the latest month of application your 61.39 endorsement can support?
check.a: April. The training must fall within the 2 calendar months before the month of application (February and March precede April) [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i)]].

chunks.title: K4b and K4c: Additional certificates and additional aircraft

body.p: The same 61.39 prerequisites apply to every certificate after the first. What changes is the endorsement set and whether a knowledge test is needed.

head: Sub-item
Typical endorsements
Notes
rows: b. Additional pilot certification (e.g., commercial, instrument rating, CFI)

Commercial: A.38 knowledge test (61.123(c)) and A.39 practical test (61.123(e)) [[12:47|AC 61-65K A.38]] [[60:310|14 CFR 61.123(c)]]. Instrument: A.42, A.43, A.44 [[12:48|AC 61-65K A.42]]. CFI airplane: A.45 FOI, A.46 knowledge, A.47 practical, A.49 spin training [[12:48|AC 61-65K A.45]] [[12:49|AC 61-65K A.49]]. Plus A.1 and A.2 [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.1]].
Initial CFI endorsements must come from an instructor who meets 61.195(h) [[12:21|AC 61-65K 26]]. The spin endorsement is required for every airplane CFI applicant [[60:339|14 CFR 61.183(i)]].
c. Additional aircraft qualification (category, class or type rating)

Additional category or class rating: A.78, attesting competence in the knowledge areas and proficiency in the areas of operation [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.78]] [[60:246|14 CFR 61.63(b)]]. Type rating: A.79 or A.80 [[12:55|AC 61-65K A.79]]. Solo before the rating: A.76 [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.76]].

No additional knowledge test if the pilot holds an airplane, rotorcraft, powered-lift, weight-shift, powered parachute or airship rating at that certificate level [[60:246|14 CFR 61.63(c)(4)]]. A class rating does not need the specified training times [[60:246|14 CFR 61.63(c)(3)]].

body.p: Additional rating applicants are already pilots; they are not student pilots and do not need a student pilot certificate. Before solo in the new aircraft they need the 61.31(d)(2) endorsement, and before the test the 61.63 endorsement [[25:202|AIH C-1]].

bullets: Additional rating applicants (other than ATP) need instructor recommendations and the appropriate endorsements [[12:29|AC 61-65K 33.1]].
Applicants adding ratings at the ATP level need no recommendation unless it is a retest [[12:30|AC 61-65K 34.2]].
Failed knowledge test: you may sign the endorsement block at the bottom of the knowledge test report after giving the additional training [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.77]] [[25:204|AIH C-3]].

check.q: A commercial ASEL pilot adds a single-engine sea rating. Knowledge test? Endorsement?
check.a: No knowledge test, since they already hold an airplane rating at that level; they need an instructor endorsement and the practical test [[60:246|14 CFR 61.63(c)]].

body.p: A flight review is at least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training, covering current part 91 rules and the maneuvers and procedures you judge necessary for safe exercise of the pilot's privileges [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]]. To act as PIC, the pilot needs a review since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month of the flight, plus a logbook endorsement from the instructor who gave it [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

head: Outcome
What you write
rows: Satisfactory

A.69: [name], [grade of pilot certificate], [certificate number] has satisfactorily completed a flight review of 61.56(a) on [date] [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]]. Log the flight and ground time too [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.2]].
Not satisfactory
No unsatisfactory endorsement is required [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]]. Log it as dual instruction given, not a failure, and recommend training on the weak areas [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].
Pilot does not meet AELS
Do not endorse completion. Log the training, advise the pilot and contact the FSDO [[12:8|AC 61-65K 11.4.2]].

bullets: You may not endorse a flight review unless you conducted it under 61.56(a) [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]].
It is a training event, not a practical test; it may take more than the 1 plus 1 hour minimum [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]].

No review needed if the pilot passed a practical test or proficiency check, completed a WINGS phase (A.70), or is a student with a current solo endorsement in the period [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)]] [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.70]].
A CFI who completed recent experience under 61.197 in the period may skip the 1 hour of ground training [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(f)]].

body.p: Before the review, interview the pilot and read the logbook for total time, time in type and recency, then agree on how the review will run and what counts as satisfactory [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.3]] [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.4]]. A summary like the RMH certification and experience table helps the pilot list current endorsements and recent experience [[30:14|RMH 2-2]].

check.q: A pilot's flight review was completed June 10, 2025. Through the end of which month may they act as PIC?
check.a: June 2027. Acting in June 2027, the 24th calendar month before is June 2025, and the review falls in it [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

chunks.title: K6: Your required records as a flight instructor

body.p: 14 CFR 61.189 requires you to keep, in a logbook or a separate document [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189(b)]]:

bullets: The name of each person whose logbook you endorsed for solo flight privileges, and the date.
The name of each person you endorsed for a knowledge test or practical test, with the kind of test, the date and the results.
Keep these records for at least 3 years [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189(c)]].

body.p: A training folder for each learner keeps lesson plans, requirements, instruction received, part 61 requirements met and solo endorsements in one place; many records are now electronic [[25:152|AIH 7-8]]. Syllabus records with boxes beside each item track progress and back up later endorsements [[25:150|AIH 7-6]].

head: Other record
Rule or guidance
rows: TSA proof of U.S. citizenship
Keep copies 5 years, or make the A.14 endorsement in the student's logbook and your own record [[12:42|AC 61-65K A.14]]
Flight review plan of action
Not required by 61.189, but you may keep it as a record of the review's scope [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3]]
Student pilot application ID
Note the ID type, number and expiration date on the 8710 [[12:14|AC 61-65K 19.3]]

callout.text: Your pass-rate record is also your recent experience evidence: 5 or more applicants endorsed in 24 calendar months with at least 80 percent passing the first time [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(b)(2)(i)]].

check.q: You endorsed a student for a practical test in March 2026. What must your record show, and until when?
check.a: The student's name, kind of test, date and result, kept until at least March 2029 [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189]].

chunks.title: K7: Recent experience, renewal and reinstatement

body.p: You may exercise CFI privileges only if, within the preceding 24 calendar months, you met one recent experience requirement. The period starts from the month the certificate was issued, the month you met the requirement, or the last month of your current period if you meet it within the 3 calendar months before that month [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(a)]].

head: Way to establish recent experience
Rule
rows: Pass a practical test for a rating on your CFI certificate or an additional CFI rating
Endorsed at least 5 applicants for practical tests in 24 calendar months, at least 80 percent passing first try
Company check pilot, chief instructor, check airman, part 121/135 instructor, or a position regularly evaluating pilots
Approved FIRC completed within the preceding 3 calendar months
Military instructor pilot or examiner proficiency check
WINGS instructor: 15 activities, 5 different pilots, endorsements made

body.p: Renewal: a certificate issued before December 1, 2024 still shows an expiration date. Renew it by establishing recent experience before the month of expiration and submitting the 8710; you get a new certificate with no expiration date [[60:352|14 CFR 61.197(e)]] [[12:28|AC 61-65K 30.4]].

Reinstatement: miss your period and you may not instruct until privileges are reinstated [[60:352|14 CFR 61.197(c)]]. Within 3 calendar months after the last month, an approved FIRC (or a (a)(2) option) works; after more than 3 calendar months, you must pass a CFI practical test for a held rating or an additional rating [[60:352|14 CFR 61.199(a)]]. Old flight instructor ratings on a pilot certificate are no longer valid [[60:353|14 CFR 61.199(b)]].

callout.text: Last month August? Do it in May, June, July or August to keep August [[12:27|AC 61-65K 30.3.2]].

A FIRC done more than 3 calendar months before your last month moves your period: it then runs 24 calendar months from the month the 8710 is submitted, and the 8710 must go in within 3 calendar months of the FIRC [[12:27|AC 61-65K 30.3.1]].

check.q: Your RE period ended in May. It is now September and you have done nothing. Can a FIRC reinstate you?
check.a: No. More than 3 calendar months have passed, so you must pass a CFI practical test [[60:352|14 CFR 61.199(a)(2)]].

chunks.title: R1: Endorsements without limitations or expiration dates

body.p: An endorsement with no limits gives the student every privilege the rule allows, including conditions you never trained. The rules expect you to write limits: a solo endorsement is subject to any limitations you consider necessary [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(d)(1)(ii)]], the student may not fly contrary to them [[60:278|14 CFR 61.89(a)(8)]], and the sample endorsements leave a space to list conditions [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.8]] [[12:42|AC 61-65K A.11]].

head: Hazard
What can go wrong
Mitigation
rows: No limitations listed
Student solos in wind, ceilings or airports you never trained
Write the wind, visibility, airport and time limits you mean [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(d)(1)]]
No date, or a stale date
Nobody can tell if the 90-day window is still open [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]]
Date every endorsement; renew solo every 90 days [[60:278|14 CFR 61.87(p)(4)]]
Time limit not stated
Night endorsement used after it lapsed
State the expiry, as A.5 does: 90 calendar days from the night training [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.5]]
No RE end date in the signature
Examiner cannot verify you were current when you signed
Generic make and model
Solo in an airplane you never checked
Name the M/M [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.6]]

body.p: The safety stakes are real. Signing solo for a learner who is not proficient, or an added rating for a pilot who does not meet the rules, is a breach of faith with that person [[25:184|AIH 9-14]]. If you doubt a learner's fitness, get another instructor's evaluation and withhold the endorsement [[25:49|AIH 2-16]].

The FAA itself can put limitations on a pilot certificate when the pilot did not show all the skills for its privileges [[1:31|PHAK 1-16]]. Your logbook limitations work the same way at the student level: they define where and when the student may fly.

check.q: Which part of 14 CFR makes your written logbook limitations binding on a student?
check.a: 61.89(a)(8): a student may not act as PIC contrary to limitations an authorized instructor placed in the logbook [[60:278|14 CFR 61.89(a)(8)]].

chunks.title: S1: How to teach it and how the examiner checks it

body.p: The examiner will ask you to describe and prepare logbook entries or endorsements for at least two events from K1 to K5 (ACS AI.II.K.S1). Practice writing them on a blank logbook page, not just reading them.

Teaching endorsements to a new instructor is a mental skill, so the demonstration-performance method fits: you explain and demonstrate one endorsement, the learner writes one under supervision, then writes one alone while you evaluate [[25:124|AIH 5-21]] [[25:125|AIH 5-22]].

bullets: Explanation: show the rule first (for example 61.87(n)), then the AC 61-65K wording that satisfies it [[25:202|AIH C-1]].
Demonstration: write A.6 for a real make and model, saying each part out loud: name, rule cited, M/M, signature block with RE date [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.6]].
Performance and supervision: the learner writes A.10 for a planned cross-country you hand them, including limits [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.10]].
Evaluation: the learner writes a flight review entry alone; you compare it with A.69 [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]].

body.p: Use guided discussion with what-if questions to reach risk: what if the student's 90 days lapse on a weekend? What if the wind exceeds your limit at the outlying field? Open questions lead to risk management and decision making [[25:119|AIH 5-16]].

callout.text: Build endorsements into your syllabus. Required endorsements and recordkeeping designed into the syllabus make training easier to track and records easier to certify [[25:129|AIH 5-26]].

check.q: In the demonstration-performance method, who works alone during the evaluation phase?
check.a: The learner works independently while the instructor judges the performance [[25:125|AIH 5-22]].

head: Error
What you see
How to fix it
rows: Old signature format
"CFI Exp." on an instructor whose certificate has no expiration date
Use the RE end date format [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]]
Bare training entry
Signature and date only
Add description, lesson length, certificate number and RE date [[60:231|14 CFR 61.51(h)(2)]]
Pre-solo test not reviewed
Graded test filed, wrong answers never discussed
Review all incorrect answers before solo [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(b)(2)]]
Lapsed solo endorsement
Last solo endorsement more than 90 days old
Fly with the student and re-endorse [[60:278|14 CFR 61.87(p)(4)]]
Cross-country signed without weather check
Per-flight endorsement signed at the counter
Review current and forecast weather first [[60:281|14 CFR 61.93(d)(2)]]
Unsatisfactory flight review written up as a failure
Logbook says "failed flight review"
Log dual given, recommend training [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]]
Too many hours
More than 8 hours of flight training in 24 consecutive hours
Stop; 8 hours is the limit [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(a)]]
No record kept
Cannot show who you endorsed for tests
Keep the 61.189 record 3 years [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189(c)]]

callout.text: A self-endorsement is never valid, even for an operating privilege like tailwheel [[60:349|14 CFR 61.195(i)]].

check.q: A flight review did not go well. What should the logbook say?
check.a: Log the time as dual instruction given, not a failure; no unsatisfactory endorsement is required [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]] [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]].

f1.alt: A strip of a pilot logbook's Remarks and Endorsements column. It reads: I certify that (First name, MI, Last name) has satisfactorily completed the presolo knowledge exam of section 61.87(b) for the (make and model aircraft). S/S [date] J.J. Jones 987654321 CFI Exp. 12-31-2007.

f2.caption: Figure C-2. This sample logbook endorsement is for completion of a flight review. (AIH C-3)
f2.alt: A logbook Remarks and Endorsements column with the entry: I certify that [First name, MI, Last name], [grade of pilot certificate], [certificate number], has satisfactorily completed a flight review of section 61.56 (a) and (c) on [date]. J.J. Jones 7654321 CFI Exp. 12-31-2022.

f3.alt: A boxed sample endorsement citing section 61.101(i). It certifies training under section 61.87 in a named make and model and that the pilot may solo on a date under listed conditions, for example flight requiring communication with ATC or flight in an aircraft for which the pilot holds no category or class rating.

Ground instruction, three one-hour blocks: flight manual operations sections, line inspection, flight deck familiarization; loading, limitations and servicing, instruments, radio and special equipment, aircraft systems; performance section, cruise control, review. scenario.title: Saturday at the flight school sign-off desk
scenario.setup: You are a CFI with an RE end date of 08-31-2027. Today (a Saturday in June 2027) three people are waiting. Maya is a student pilot whose C172 solo endorsement is 85 days old; she wants to fly a solo cross-country to an airport 60 NM away, and she asks you for your first sign-off with her because her usual CFI is sick. Raj is ready for his private pilot checkride next Thursday; his last dual lesson was in April. Ellen, a private pilot, wants a flight review and a high-performance endorsement in her new 230 hp airplane. Winds at the destination are forecast 15 gusting 25.

questions.q: Can you sign Maya's per-flight cross-country endorsement even though you are not her regular instructor?
questions.a: Yes. The 61.93(c)(3) endorsement need not come from her usual instructor, but you must make sure the 61.93(c)(1) and (2) endorsements are already in her logbook [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.6]].

questions.q: What else must you check before letting Maya go?
questions.a: Her planning, the current and forecast weather (flight can be completed under VFR), her proficiency, the make and model cross-country endorsement and a current solo endorsement [[60:281|14 CFR 61.93(d)]]. Her solo endorsement is 85 days old, so it lapses in days; plan to re-endorse after flying with her [[60:278|14 CFR 61.87(p)(4)]].

questions.q: The gusts exceed what her instructor's solo endorsement allows. What then?
questions.a: She may not fly contrary to limitations in her logbook [[60:278|14 CFR 61.89(a)(8)]]. If the endorsement has no written limits, that is the R1 hazard: add limits you consider necessary [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(d)(1)]].

questions.q: Raj's last training was in April and the test is in June. Can you sign his 61.39 endorsement today without flying?
questions.a: Yes for training: April is within the 2 calendar months before a June application [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i)]]. But you must also find him prepared and review his knowledge test deficiencies (A.1, A.2) and sign the 8710 recommendation only after a full ACS-level demonstration [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.1]] [[25:183|AIH 9-13]].

questions.q: Which endorsements do you give Ellen, and do you need two separate entries?
questions.a: A.69 for the flight review (only if satisfactory) and A.73 for high performance after ground and flight training in that airplane [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]] [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.73]]. They certify different rules, 61.56 and 61.31(f), so write both [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(f)(1)(ii)]].

questions.q: What goes in your own records from today, and how long do you keep it?
questions.a: Maya's solo endorsement if you re-endorse her, with the date, and Raj's practical test endorsement with the kind of test, date and later the result; keep them at least 3 years [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189]].

skills.do: The examiner will have you "Describe and prepare logbook entries/endorsements required for at least two of the events specified in the elements or sub-elements of K1 through K5" (ACS AI.II.K.S1). Expect to write them on paper with the correct rule, make and model, limits and a signature block with your RE end date.
skills.practice: On blank logbook pages, write A.3, A.6, A.10, A.37 with A.1 and A.2, and A.69 from memory, then check each against AC 61-65K [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]] [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.6]] [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]]. Have a fellow instructor give you a scenario and you choose the endorsements.

quiz.q: Under 61.51(h), which item must a training entry include?
options: A description of the training and the lesson length
The aircraft's Hobbs start and stop times
The student's total time to date
quiz.why: Training time must be endorsed legibly and include a description of the training, its length, and the instructor's signature, certificate number and expiration or RE end date [[60:231|14 CFR 61.51(h)(2)]].

quiz.q: Who must administer the 61.87(b) pre-solo knowledge test?
quiz.why: The student's authorized instructor administers it and reviews all incorrect answers [[60:271|14 CFR 61.87(b)(2)]].

quiz.q: A student holds a current C172 solo endorsement. May she solo a PA-28 today?
options: Yes, if it has fewer than 200 hp
No, the endorsement is for the specific make and model
quiz.why: The 90-day solo endorsement is for the specific make and model to be flown [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]].

quiz.q: Solo to an airport inside Class B airspace requires training where?
options: At the specific airport, with the endorsement dated within 90 days
In the Class C airspace nearby
quiz.why: Ground and flight training at that specific airport and an endorsement dated within the 90 days before the flight [[60:287|14 CFR 61.95(b)]].

quiz.q: How often must the complex airplane endorsement be renewed?
quiz.why: 61.31(e) calls for a one-time endorsement [[60:213|14 CFR 61.31(e)(1)(ii)]].

quiz.q: The 61.39 practical test endorsement certifies training within what period?
options: 2 calendar months before the month of application
quiz.why: Training received and logged within 2 calendar months preceding the month of application [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i)]].

quiz.q: A commercial ASEL pilot adds a multiengine class rating. Does she take another knowledge test?
options: No, she already holds an airplane rating at that level
Only if she lacks an instrument rating
quiz.why: No additional knowledge test if the applicant holds an airplane rating at that certificate level [[60:246|14 CFR 61.63(c)(4)]].

quiz.q: Minimum time for a flight review?
options: 1 hour of flight and 1 hour of ground training
quiz.why: At least 1 hour of flight training and 1 hour of ground training [[60:236|14 CFR 61.56(a)]].

quiz.q: How long must you keep 61.189 records?
Your RE period ended 5 calendar months ago. How do you reinstate?
quiz.why: After more than 3 calendar months, a CFI practical test for a held or additional rating is required [[60:352|14 CFR 61.199(a)(2)]].

final_quiz.q: A student lands at a towered field 40 NM away with your per-flight endorsement. The tower changes runways and she wants to divert to a third airport you never named. What applies?
options: She may land anywhere within 50 NM
Except in an emergency, she may land only at airports her endorsements allow
She may land anywhere with a current solo endorsement
The tower can authorize the new airport
final_quiz.why: Unless there is an emergency, no student may make a solo landing anywhere other than airports allowed by the 61.93 endorsements [[12:17|AC 61-65K 20.12]].

final_quiz.q: An applicant failed the private knowledge test. You give two ground lessons. What lets him retest?
options: Nothing; he can retest after 30 days
An endorsement from the instructor who gave the additional training
A new 8710 signed by the chief instructor
final_quiz.why: He needs the training and an endorsement from the authorized instructor who gave it [[60:227|14 CFR 61.49(a)]]; you may use the block on the knowledge test report [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.77]].

final_quiz.q: Your RE period ends in August 2027. You complete a FIRC and submit the 8710 in June 2027. When does your new period end?
final_quiz.why: Done within the 3 calendar months before the last month, the period runs from that last month, so August 2029 [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(a)(3)]] [[12:27|AC 61-65K 30.3.2]].

final_quiz.q: Your RE period ends August 31. You finish a FIRC on January 5 and submit the 8710 on April 13. When does the new period end?
final_quiz.why: This is the AC's Example 3: 24 calendar months from April 30, so April 30 two years later [[12:27|AC 61-65K 30.3.2]].

final_quiz.q: You have already given 7.0 hours of flight training since this time yesterday. A student asks for a 1.5 hour flight. What may you do?
options: Fly 1.5 hours; ground time is separate
Fly 1.5 hours if one is a flight review
final_quiz.why: No more than 8 hours of flight training in any 24 consecutive hours, so 1.0 hour remains [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(a)]].

final_quiz.q: A new CFI just finished tailwheel training with a friend who is not an instructor and wants to sign his own tailwheel endorsement. Your advice?
options: Fine, CFIs may endorse themselves for operating privileges
Prohibited; a CFI may not self-endorse an operating privilege
final_quiz.why: 61.195(i) prohibits any self-endorsement for an operating privilege [[60:349|14 CFR 61.195(i)]], and the training must come from an authorized instructor [[60:215|14 CFR 61.31(i)]].

final_quiz.q: A private ASEL pilot is training for a helicopter add-on and wants to solo the helicopter before the checkride. What does he need?
options: A 61.31(d)(2) solo endorsement after the required training
Nothing; he is already a pilot
A 61.87 pre-solo test and student certificate
final_quiz.why: Additional rating applicants are not student pilots; before solo they need the 61.31(d)(2) endorsement [[25:202|AIH C-1]] [[12:54|AC 61-65K A.76]].

final_quiz.q: A commercial applicant's knowledge test report lists four deficient areas. Which endorsement shows you covered them?
final_quiz.why: The 61.39 endorsement must certify satisfactory knowledge of the deficient areas [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(iii)]] [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.2]].

final_quiz.q: You sign a student's solo endorsement with no limitations. She flies solo in a crosswind beyond anything you trained. What was the root error?
options: You gave an endorsement without the limitations you considered necessary
The endorsement needed a TSA entry
final_quiz.why: You must judge her safe under known circumstances, subject to the limits you list [[60:346|14 CFR 61.195(d)(1)(ii)]]; she is then bound by them [[60:278|14 CFR 61.89(a)(8)]].

final_quiz.q: A student got night pattern and night navigation training at her home airport 95 days ago. Can she fly solo at night there tonight?
options: No, the training and endorsement must be within the 90 days before the flight
Yes, if her day solo endorsement is current
final_quiz.why: Night solo requires the endorsement from the instructor who gave the training within the 90-day period before the flight [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(o)(3)]].

final_quiz.q: A pilot logged PIC time in a 260 hp airplane in 1994 and now buys one. What endorsement does he need for high performance?
options: None; pre-August 4, 1997 PIC time is an exception
final_quiz.why: The training and endorsement are not required with high-performance PIC time logged before August 4, 1997 [[60:214|14 CFR 61.31(f)(2)(i)]].

final_quiz.q: During a flight review the pilot cannot understand your English instructions well enough to meet the AELS. What do you do?
options: Endorse it and note the language issue
Do not endorse completion; log training received, advise the pilot and contact the FSDO
Sign it if the flying was good
final_quiz.why: That is the AC 61-65K procedure for a pilot who does not meet the AELS on a flight review [[12:8|AC 61-65K 11.4.2]].

final_quiz.q: A student's 50 NM repeated cross-country endorsement names one route. He wants to fly it three times this week. What does he need each time?
options: A new per-flight endorsement each time
No separate per-flight endorsements, but current solo and cross-country endorsements
final_quiz.why: For repeated flights within 50 NM, separate endorsements are not required for each flight, but he still needs the solo and solo cross-country endorsements [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(b)(2)]].

takeaways: Every endorsement: legible, signed, dated, certificate number, and RE end date.
Training given: describe it, give its length, and sign it.
Solo: specific make and model, 90-day clock, written limits; review every wrong pre-solo answer.
Solo cross-country: category and M/M endorsements plus one per flight after you check planning and weather.
Practical test: training within 2 calendar months before the month of application, deficiencies reviewed, 8710 recommendation only after a full ACS demonstration.
Flight review: endorse only satisfactory reviews; otherwise log dual given.
Keep 61.189 records 3 years and keep your own recent experience inside its 24 calendar months.
cfi_notes: AIH 9-13 says the 8710-1 recommendation is valid for 60 days and should match the logbook endorsement date [[25:183|AIH 9-13]]. 14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i) and AC 61-65K use training within 2 calendar months preceding the month of application [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i)]] [[12:10|AC 61-65K 14]]. Teach the CFR wording.

The sample endorsements in AIH Figures C-1 and C-2 use "CFI Exp." signature blocks [[25:203|AIH C-2]] [[25:204|AIH C-3]]. Certificates issued since December 1, 2024 carry no expiration date; use the RE end date format in AC 61-65K [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].

AIH 7-8 says good records help an instructor who needs to renew a certificate [[25:152|AIH 7-8]]. Under the current rule it is recent experience under 61.197, and only pre-December 2024 certificates are renewed [[60:352|14 CFR 61.197(e)]].
14 CFR 61.87(n) says "90 days" [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(n)]] while AC 61-65K says "90 calendar days" [[12:15|AC 61-65K 20.3]]. Teach students to count conservatively and re-endorse early.

PHAK Figure 1-21 cites 61.101(i) for the recreational solo endorsement [[1:32|PHAK 1-17]]; AC 61-65K A.34 cites 61.101(j), the paragraph that requires the endorsement [[12:46|AC 61-65K A.34]]. Both refer to the same pair of paragraphs; quote the AC.

AIH C-1 describes 61.189 as recording the type, name and date of every endorsement [[25:203|AIH C-2]]; the CFR itself names solo endorsements and test endorsements [[60:344|14 CFR 61.189(b)]]. Keeping all of them is good practice and costs nothing.

Have new instructors write endorsements on paper during ground lessons. The S1 element is about preparing them, and most errors examiners see are missing pieces: make and model, limits, date or RE end date.
When a pilot's checkout is insufficient for sign-off, debrief every problem area and schedule more training or refer them to another instructor [[25:205|AIH C-4]].
The night solo sample A.5 states its own expiry: 90 calendar days from the night training [[12:41|AC 61-65K A.5]]. Copy that habit and write the time limit into any time-limited endorsement.
gaps: The sources do not show the 8710-1 or IACRA instructor recommendation screens; practice in IACRA with a real applicant or a training account.
The only SFAR endorsements in AC 61-65K are for SFAR 73 (Robinson R-22/R-44 helicopters). The sources give no airplane SFAR endorsement; read the SFAR itself if one applies.
No source here defines how close a "similar make and model" must be for 61.87 pre-solo training; that is the instructor's judgment and school policy.
The sources do not list which limitations to write in a solo endorsement (wind, visibility, airports); AIH C-1 says only that you may add requirements. Your school and your judgment decide.
AC 61-98E says the instructor may keep the flight review plan of action, but no source sets a retention time for it or for electronic logbook signatures.

activities.title: Parts of an endorsement
activities.intro: Drag each name to its numbered pin.

pins.label: Make and model the test covered
Old expiration-date format (now RE end date)

activities.title: From first lesson to first solo
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Give and log pre-solo flight training in the make and model
Review every incorrect answer with the student
Judge proficiency and safety on the 61.87 maneuvers
Endorse pre-solo knowledge (A.3) and pre-solo training (A.4)
Endorse solo for the specific make and model with your limits (A.6)

activities.title: How long does it last?
activities.intro: Tap an endorsement, then tap where it belongs.
buckets: Dated within 90 days before the flight
Covers one flight or one named route
One-time, no time limit in the rule

items.t: Student solo in a make and model (61.87(n))
Student solo in Class B airspace (61.95(a))
Repeated cross-countries within 50 NM over one route (61.93(b)(2))

activities.title: Checkride paperwork and its rule
activities.intro: Tap an endorsement, then the regulation it satisfies.

pairs.l: Training within 2 calendar months, prepared for the test

activities.title: True or false: flight reviews and logbooks
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: If a flight review is unsatisfactory, you must write an unsatisfactory endorsement.
cards.why: False. No logbook entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance is required [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.69]]; log it as dual given [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]].

cards.s: A pilot who passed a CFI practical test within the period does not need a separate flight review.
cards.why: True. A practical test for a flight instructor certificate satisfies 61.56 [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(d)(2)]].

cards.s: A flight review may take more than 1 hour of flight and 1 hour of ground training.
cards.why: True. The FAA reminds instructors that it may require more [[15:22|AC 61-98E 4.1.1]].

cards.s: You may endorse a pilot's flight review that another instructor conducted.
cards.why: False. You may not endorse a flight review unless you conducted it [[60:347|14 CFR 61.195(d)(5)]].

cards.s: A CFI who met 61.197 recent experience in the period may skip the 1 hour of ground training on a flight review.
A student with a current solo endorsement needs a flight review to act as PIC on solo flights.
cards.why: False. A student training for a certificate with a current solo endorsement is exempt [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(g)]].

activities.title: Count the months and the numbers
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: In the last 24 calendar months you endorsed 7 applicants for practical tests. How many must have passed on the first attempt for the 80 percent recent experience option?
items.why: 80 percent of 7 = 5.6, so at least 6 must pass (6/7 = 86 percent; 5/7 = 71 percent is too few) [[60:351|14 CFR 61.197(b)(2)(i)]].

items.q: A student's last logged practical test training was March 20. What is the latest month (1 to 12) in which she can apply for the test on that training?
items.why: Applying in May, the 2 preceding calendar months are March and April, so March training counts. In June they would be April and May [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(i)]].

items.q: Your recent experience period's last month is August. What is the earliest month (1 to 12) you can complete a recent experience requirement and keep August as your last month?
items.why: Within the 3 calendar months preceding the last month, plus the last month itself: May, June, July or August [[12:27|AC 61-65K 30.3.2]].

items.q: You have given 3.2 and 2.9 hours of flight training in the last 24 hours. How many more hours of flight training may you give in that period?
You endorsed a student for solo in June 2026. Until what year must you keep that 61.189 record at the least?

activities.title: Sign or don't sign
activities.intro: You are a CFI at a busy school with an RE end date of 08-31-2027. It is a Monday morning and four logbooks are on your desk.

steps.s: Logbook 1: a student you have never flown with wants solo in a PA-28. Her C172 solo endorsement is current from another CFI.
options: Write a PA-28 solo endorsement now
Fly with her in the PA-28 first; endorse only if she is proficient in it
Her C172 endorsement covers the PA-28
Have her take the pre-solo test again only
steps.why: You must have given training in that or a similar make and model and found her proficient before endorsing the specific make and model [[60:277|14 CFR 61.87(p)]] [[60:278|14 CFR 61.87(p)(3)]].

steps.s: Logbook 2: a student's per-flight cross-country request. The forecast shows marginal VFR at the destination after 3 PM; he plans to land at 2:30.
options: Sign it; the arrival is before 3 PM
Sign it with written limits on departure time and weather, after confirming the flight can be completed under VFR
Refuse all solo cross-countries in MVFR seasons
steps.why: You must determine the flight can be completed under VFR [[60:281|14 CFR 61.93(d)(2)]], and the endorsement states any limits you require [[60:280|14 CFR 61.93(c)(3)(iii)]].

steps.s: Logbook 3: a private pilot asks for a tailwheel endorsement after three lessons. Wheel landings went well, but you never practiced a go-around.
options: Fly a lesson that includes go-arounds, then endorse
Sign it with a limit of no go-arounds
steps.why: Tailwheel training must include normal and crosswind takeoffs and landings, wheel landings and go-around procedures [[60:215|14 CFR 61.31(i)]].

steps.s: Logbook 4: an applicant's commercial checkride is tomorrow. You notice you never wrote A.2 for his knowledge test deficiencies.
options: Review the deficient areas with him, then write A.2
Sign A.2 without reviewing; he passed the test
steps.why: The 61.39 endorsement must certify satisfactory knowledge of the deficient areas [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)(iii)]] [[12:40|AC 61-65K A.2]], and examiners rely on it as proof the review was given [[25:203|AIH C-2]].
